cards.text: Two years ago, David's son Amnon violated his sister Tamar (2 Sam 13:14). Her brother Absalom, another of David's sons, never said a word to Amnon after that, good or bad, because he hated him (2 Sam 13:22). Now it's two years later, and Absalom's sheepshearers are at Baal-hazor near Ephraim.

cards.question: Absalom sends out invitations to his sheepshearing at Baal-hazor. Who does he invite?

answers.text: All the sons of the king

cards.question: Then Absalom goes to the king himself. True or false: Absalom asks King David and his servants to come with him.
David tells Absalom they shouldn't all go. What reason does David give?

answers.text: They would be a burden to Absalom
The road to Ephraim is too long
The king's work keeps him at home

cards.text: Absalom urges him, but David still won't go. He gives Absalom his blessing instead, so Absalom tries a different ask.

cards.question: If the king won't come, Absalom wants one brother there by name. “If not,” said Absalom, “please let my brother ___ go with us.”
David answers Absalom's request for Amnon with a question of his own. What does David ask?

answers.text: Why should he go with you

cards.text: Absalom urges him again, and the king sends Amnon and the rest of his sons. But Absalom has already given his young men orders about Amnon.

cards.question: Absalom tells his young men to watch Amnon and wait before they strike. What are they waiting for?

answers.text: Until Amnon's heart is merry with wine
Until Amnon falls asleep in his tent
Until the last sheep has been sheared

cards.question: Absalom's young men are being told to strike down a son of the king. True or false: Absalom tells them not to be afraid, because he is the one commanding them.

cards.text: So Absalom's young men do to Amnon just as Absalom ordered. Amnon is dead.

cards.question: The rest of the king's sons get up, and each one flees on his ___.

cards.text: The king's sons are still on the road when a report reaches David first.

cards.question: While the king's sons are still on the way, what does the report tell David?

answers.text: Absalom has struck down all the king's sons
Amnon has struck down his brother Absalom
Robbers have attacked the king's sons

cards.question: True or false: when David hears the report, he stands up, tears his clothes and lies down on the ground.

cards.text: All his servants stand by with their clothes torn. Then Jonadab speaks up, the son of David's brother Shimeah, the same shrewd friend who told Amnon how to get Tamar to come to him (2 Sam 13:3-5).

cards.question: The king is on the ground in grief. What does Jonadab tell him?
Jonadab tells David that Absalom planned this. Since when?

answers.text: Since the day Amnon violated Tamar
Since the day the shearers were hired
Since the day David blessed him

cards.text: Jonadab says it again: “Only Amnon is dead.” Friend, that report picked up a LOT on the road.
Meanwhile, Absalom has fled. The young man standing watch looks up and sees many people coming down the road west of him, along the side of the hill.

cards.question: The watchman reports men coming from the direction of Horonaim. True or false: Jonadab tells the king it's the king's sons, just as he said.
As Jonadab finishes speaking, the king's sons come in ___ loudly.

cards.text: The king and all his servants weep very bitterly too. And Absalom flees to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur, who is the father of Absalom's mother Maacah (2 Sam 3:3).

cards.question: Absalom is gone to Geshur, and David mourns for his son every ___.
Absalom has fled to Geshur. How long does he stay there?

cards.text: Over that time, David is consoled over Amnon's death.

cards.question: Now that he's been consoled over Amnon's death, true or false: King David longs to go to Absalom.

cards.text: A son in Geshur, a father whose heart keeps pulling that way, and that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this family's story is far from over.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "please let my brother ___ go with us.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's voice is nearly absent. Stop 1 has no humor, no LOUD moments, no reactions and no self-deprecation; its story cards read as plain retelling. Stop 2 has only one joke (card 7). The cards are stripped down rather than carrying his personality.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Several story cards are stripped down to bare plot without Papa Dorin's voice. Examples are stop 1 card 11 ("So Absalom's young men do to Amnon just as Absalom ordered. Amnon is dead."), stop 2 card 1 and stop 2 card 14.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: "Over that time, David is consoled over Amnon's death" ties David's consolation to Absalom's three years in Geshur. 2 Samuel 13:39 says only that he had been consoled, with no time given and no link to the three years.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card draws on 2 Samuel 13:14 and 13:22, both from before this passage, as well as 13:23. Its verses field is "2 Samuel 13:22-23": it includes one outside verse (13:22) but leaves out the other (13:14). Other cards that use outside verses (stop 2 card 4 uses 13:3-5, and stop 2 card 11 uses 3:3) cite only in-passage verses in the field and give the outside references inline. Citing 13:14-23 would take in verses the card doesn't use.
findings.question: When a story card uses verses from outside the passage and gives their references inline, should its verses field include those outside verses, or only the passage verses the card tells?

findings.problem: All five true or false cards have True as the right answer (stop 1 cards 3 and 10, stop 2 cards 3, 9 and 15). A baker who notices this can answer every true or false card without reasoning.
findings.question: Should a walkthrough vary which true or false cards are true and which are false, so the answer isn't predictable?
